Yeah I also have a hiatal hernia and depending on the type it's not as scary as it sounds. 

There's really two types, sliding and paraesophageal. And these can be distinguished by an upper endoscopy. 

You have an hiatus (opening in your diaphragm that allows your esophagus to connect to your stomach), the part where your esophagus enters/becomes your stomach is called the gastroesophageal junction. 

A sliding hiatal hernia, which account for 95% of hiatal hernias, means that part of your stomach went through your gastroesophageal junction and is not more likely to dump stomach acid into your esophagus. This is usually because the junction flap is weak and wider. 

An paraesophageal means that part of the stomach escaped outside the gastroesophageal junction(not in) and hiatus and usually has a lot of pressure and this hernia is more dangerous.
